terms.gloss: go under; come up to; undergo, take upon oneself
evidence: Cic. Rosc. Am. 31: omnēs terrōrēs perīculaque omnia succurram atque subībō (Lewis & Short)
Caes. BG 1.36: tēctum nōn subīssent (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The figure is of stooping under a load: of danger, pain and wrong a favourite expression of Cicero’s (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: omnēs terrōrēs perīculaque omnia succurram atque subībō
phrases.english: I will meet every terror and take every danger upon myself

phrases.latin: quī inter annōs XIV tēctum nōn subīssent
phrases.english: who had not come under a roof in fourteen years

sources: Lewis & Short: subeo
